Done, all four parts.

1. STALE BEADS RECONCILED. PKIX-77k9.1 (was P1), PKIX-gphz, PKIX-qws.1/.2/.3 closed as stale -- RSA-PSS, Ed25519 and P-521 are all dispatched in pkix-path/src/verifiers.rs. PKIX-qws.4 (legacy SHA-1) deliberately left open and flagged not-to-action, since SHA-1 is refused by design.

2. THE DECISION IMPLEMENTED. pkix-path default = ["rustcrypto"] (758ce9f1), published as pkix-path 0.4.2. Named as the umbrella feature so one place says what the full set is. Constrained environments now turn backends OFF -- default-features = false plus whatever a regulator permits -- and that path is tested: --no-default-features alone, and with rsa, rsa+p256, p256+p384, all check.

3. REGULATED ENVIRONMENTS CONFIRMED, not assumed (dd45bada). pkix-chain/tests/regulated_algorithms.rs, four tests. An algorithm a build will not perform arrives as SignatureNotVerified { reason: UnsupportedAlgorithm }, a curve as UnsupportedKey, a bad key as MalformedKey, and a genuinely invalid signature as SignatureInvalid -- so the four stay distinguishable at the pkix_chain::Error boundary, which is what a FIPS operator needs to avoid chasing a non-existent attack.

Two findings from writing that test, both worth keeping:
- The error arrives as PathBuild(NoValidPath { last_error, .. }), not Path(..), because verify_chain treats an unverifiable signature as AIA-recoverable and attempts reassembly first. That is correct: in a cross-signed topology an alternative issuer may sign with an algorithm this build does support.
- Which means the guarantee DEPENDS on NoValidPath.last_error being typed (PKIX-rm8.29 / PKIX-wnnn.5, done earlier the same day). While it was a Display-rendered String, a regulated deployment would have got prose to grep rather than a variant to match. Had those two beads not landed first, this one could not have been satisfied.

4. INCIDENTAL FIXED. pkix-difftest Cargo.toml no longer claims the umbrella is "rsa + p256 + p384 only" or that Ed25519 is unimplemented. baseline-limbo-analysis.md left alone as the historical capture it is.

One regression along the way, caught by CI and fixed in 2a33baf5: the new default broke x86_64-unknown-none via curve25519-dalek SIMD selection. Extended the bare-metal job existing sha2 soft-backend flag rather than relaxing the gate, since that job exists precisely so "a crate that cannot hold the claim fails here rather than in someone firmware build". thumbv7em and riscv64 were unaffected.

Gates green: fmt, clippy, rustdoc, typos, 2364 tests, workspace feature powerset clean.
